submitted.rationale: Index 29 (Sb 0.847) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0080 %. The whole Co-Sb line appears to be almost inactive at 2.7 eV: every measured value is within about ±0.01 % of zero.

rejected.reason: Stoichiometric trirutile CoSb2O6 (on the MACE hull) measured -0.0086 %, effectively zero.
Co-rich region near the Co7Sb2O12 spinel measured 0.0038 %, lower than index 29.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts trirutile CoSb2O6 on the hull (0 eV/atom), so index 20 (Sb 0.669) should be phase-pure. MEGNet predicts a 0.37 eV HSE gap. That is probably an underestimate for this correlated Co2+ oxide. It is not disqualifying at 2.7 eV illumination, but I treat it as uncertain.

Moderate support for the Sb-rich end. MEGNet gives a 1.77 eV gap for Sb2O5, which absorbs at 2.7 eV and would mix with trirutile. It predicts about 0 eV for Co3O4 (metallic-like), which argues against the Co-rich end. Co7Sb2O12 is about 0.03 eV above the hull with a 1.44 eV gap, so it stays a fallback.

Weak support. Both the trirutile and Sb-rich compositions gave EQE of about 0, so the Co-rich spinel region is the last unexplored area. Co5SbO8 (0.83 eV) and Co7Sb2O12 (1.44 eV, near the hull) have finite gaps and absorb at 2.7 eV. Index 5 (Sb 0.208) sits near Co7Sb2O12.
